author: Link1565v2
quote:
An excellent update to what I consider to be the greatest game ever made. The attention to detail is amazing. Fixing things like Zora's Domain unfreezing after beating the water temple, even small things like helping those Kokiri children cut grass or remove the rocks actually pays off now, whereas before there was no real acknowledgement. I'd say 99 percent of the changes are for the better.

The game is definitely easier than the original. Some of that comes down to the benefit of 30 years of controller innovation. Others down to design. They removed some of the tediousness of the old game by introducing Deku Scrub Seeds, which allows you to stock up on some critical items, rather than having to backtrack to get hearts etc. Some people don't like this change, but for me there's a difference between tediousness and game difficulty.

Some minor gripes I have are with some of the small changes.
I was always a fan of Navi's line "How can Hyrule's destiny depend on such a lazy boy!"
That's cut from the remake. Characters are like Mido seem a lot less hostile towards the Link. The change of wording when you get the Kokiri Sword, in the original it was a cheeky reference to the fact you are stealing it. Also the sign in Mido's house that you can take his rupees, so you know you're not stealing them. The Guard at Death Mountain is a lot nicer to you in the remake. Which kind of kills the moment when you give him the Keaton Mask and his realisation you did something nice, even though he was being an a-hole.
Shiek's voice lines and character design really give away the twist of the character early.
They toned down the shadow temple and under the well dungeons, removing the blood. It's no longer implied that the guard in the back alley dies.
Little nitpicks that take away some of the darker tone from the game. Ocarina of Time was never an overly dark game, but what was there hasn't been totally preserved here (or in the 3ds version to be fair).

But then positives farm outweigh the negatives. While I absolutely love the original and the 3DS version, I still believe this is the definitive way to play. Hyrule is stunningly beautiful, the lighting effects, even the effects on plants and grass when you cut them. Phenomenonal stuff.

Nintendo, I'm begging you, please give Majora's Mask the same love (but please keep the dark elements, it's far more important to MM).
game_title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

author: Link1565v2
quote:
Just buy the sims or one of those Steam dating sim games. This isn't GTA. 
Yeah, the map looks great, some of the simulation stuff is great. But it's supposed to be an escapist, satirical crime simulator. No one, not one single person, before release was saying "man I hope there's a mission where I get to paint walls, buy tampons and assemble furniture!". Arguments that it's optional fall flat, considering it affects the outcome of the game if you don't do it. And arguments that it's just the first half of the game also fall flat, why am I wading through all this filler garbage with these extremely boring characters to get to the good stuff? GTA V started with an excellent mission. Most GTAs have compelling intros. GTA VI is a movie pretending to be a game. 

Moving the game away from letting you randomly rampage (translation: have fun) to "more focused" violence is a braindead move. Having areas and times where you can't steal cars in a game called GRAND THEFT AUTO is just ridiculous.

There are a lot of people who way overspent on scalped PS5s and the $100 usd price tag for this game. They need to gaslight themselves that it's good. But it isn't. Is it the worst game ever made? No. Is it worth the hype and price tag? Also no. 

We can kill animals in this game, but no we can't kill certain npcs that are walking propaganda statements, because that'd be bad for Take Two's bottom line if they broke BlackRock DEI rules.

It's corporate slop. Very sleak, very pretty. But slop nonetheless.

A trojan horse for talentless hack, activist writers who knew this game would make a bajillion dollars regardless of quality. Rockstar is not the company it once was. The overwhelming success of GTA V broke them. They sold out years ago, and now they're far too financially critical to TTI to take the kinds of risks they could in the PS2 era. 

While financially it was always going to be a win. Making it a critical win would have been easy (and I'm not talking about the paid off/curated critics). They actually had to put effort into making it bad. That's the frustrating part. Literally all they needed to do was copy/paste GTA V into a Vice City setting. Done, easy. There'd be none of this culture war argument about it. But as usual, the big companies couldn't help but let the activists take control. 

If you haven't made the mistake of already buying it. Wait for PC where mods will hopefully fix all the BS. Although I'm sure there will be a concerted effort from Rockstar and websites like Nexus to prevent modders from fixing the problems with this corpo slopfest.

PS: the people coming from here to review bomb Ocarina of Time are a perfect example of the copium and self-gaslighting these people are doing to themselves. They can't stand that others aren't clapping like seals for the multi billion dollar corporation and are daring to criticise the game they've poured the last 13 years of their hopes and dreams into. It's not the game that was promised. People noticed. That's reality, get over it.
